final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence and instead reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is partly valid: the admissible evidence does support operational readiness and contradicts any claim that monitoring and rollback alone make the launch compliant. But the key audit concern remains unresolved. Under the policy and the cited evidence, certification is compliant only if the material limitation is resolved, the affected use case is excluded, approved risk acceptance exists, or pre-launch disclosure is confirmed. None of those predicates is proven in the admissible record. That is why this remains suspicious rather than compliant_with_caveats: the proposed caveat is not merely a disclosure note on an otherwise satisfied record; it is itself an unproven condition required for compliance. The Actor's narrower explanation improves precision, but it does not cure the evidentiary gap.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the required launch-time disclosure has been prepared, approved, or attached to the release packet before launch.
The affected retirement plan servicing segment remains exposed in the initial rollout and is not excluded by the rollout gate.
The only risk-acceptance artifact is incomplete, unapproved, and does not address the exposed retirement plan servicing segment.
Policy text states that rollout percentage, monitoring, and rollback do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
A caveated certification theory still depends on an unresolved compliance predicate: confirmed pre-launch disclosure, approved risk acceptance, or exclusion of the affected use case.
